A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIT-BO research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–H, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original optimization performance, runtime measurements, statistical rankings and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmarking results and adds surrogate diagnostics, expanded ablations and shifted-function experiments in Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: Appendix B.8 adds an experimentally tested adaptation that fine-tunes TabPFN on task-specific data before using it in GIT-BO. This is a limited training-procedure extension; Algorithm 1's default frozen surrogate, gradient-informed subspace, centroid anchor and UCB search remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix B.9 adds shifted-optimum scenarios for five 100D synthetic functions, changing the input environment tested. The original 60-problem suite and embedded-subspace problems remain. The abstract's correction from ten to eleven real-world tasks does not represent added coverage: both benchmark inventories already contain eleven.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set is retained, but the within-TabPFN comparison expands substantially. v3's full-space versus GI-subspace comparison becomes comparisons including TabPFN with trust regions and BAxUS projections, crossed with EI and UCB, in v4 Appendices B.4–B.5. Appendix C also replaces the untuned GP comparator configuration with a Hvarfner-style Vanilla GP configuration.

E3.justification: v4 adds initialization-size experiments with 20, 50, 200 and 1000 samples, fine-tuning with 1000 separate samples for 100 epochs, and predictive-mean comparisons over context sizes 10–5000. The expanded subspace/acquisition ablation uses 100D synthetic functions instead of v3's 500D versions, and Appendix C changes GP settings. Appendix G.1 also revises the reported CPU allocation from 22 to 24 cores; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands tests of the method's design and robustness: alternative projection controls, centroid versus incumbent anchoring, initialization sensitivity, surrogate fine-tuning, shifted optima and a TabPFN–GP approximation diagnostic. It revises the GP subspace-recovery analysis while retaining the existing subspace-dimension, exploration-factor and sampling sweeps.

E5.justification: The main 20-seed protocol, 95% confidence intervals and Friedman/Wilcoxon/Holm procedures remain. v4 explicitly reports ten trials for Appendices B.4–B.8, while its revised subspace/acquisition plots omit uncertainty bands visible in v3 Figure 6. Figure 7's retained curves are described as average rather than median regret, without evidence of recomputation.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial diagnostic, sensitivity, fine-tuning and shifted-function results, including runtime Table 3. Appendix C replaces the poor GP subspace-recovery findings with successful recovery for Branin and Ackley and a one-dimension error for Levy under changed GP settings. Figure 2(c) changes GIT-BO's synthetic rank from 1.93 to 1.69 and BAxUS's from 1.69 to 1.93, contradicting the retained text naming BAxUS best. Most original benchmark convergence plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.9 adds an algebraic argument about origin containment: BAxUS includes the origin through its linear embedding, whereas the centroid-offset GI subspace need not. The existing formal assumptions, lemmas, regret theorem and convergence bound are otherwise retained. The new approximation diagnostic is empirical evidence, not an additional proof.

C1.justification: The introduction adds the claim that GI-subspace guidance improves both TFM-based and GP-based BO, broadening the stated contribution beyond the earlier TFM emphasis. The central claims about frozen-surrogate optimization, competitive performance across 60 problems and scaling to 500 dimensions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C reverses its interpretation from unreliable GP gradients limiting GI-subspace effectiveness to generalizability across surrogate types, with residual threshold sensitivity. v4 also adds explanations involving centroid stability, isotropic trust-region limitations, task adaptation and origin bias. Section 3.2 reinterprets the gradient matrix as predictive-model sensitivity rather than posterior covariance.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the future code-release promise with a stated public repository link and adds fine-tuning and BoTorch gradient-propagation details. It corrects the CPU allocation, changes the total-compute unit from hours to seconds and corrects the backward-call name. The promised PyPI benchmark release disappears; most existing implementation and preprocessing documentation remains.

R1.justification: v4 adds literature connecting the method to empirical-Fisher approximations, Fisher spectral structure, EI numerical stability and tabular-model adaptation, including Ament, Kunstner and Real-TabPFN references. These extend supporting connections while retaining the central positioning around foundation-model surrogates and active subspaces. The Li preprint-to-publication update concerns an existing cited work.

P1.justification: v4 adds an introductory ablation paragraph and a six-part results summary, reorganizes Appendix B and rewrites parts of Appendices A and C. It also standardizes terminology and updates publication headers and acknowledgments. The main section structure and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the visual evidence with diagnostic and ablation figures and a runtime table, replacing the original combined acquisition/subspace display with expanded comparisons. Figure 2 is redrawn in color, and Appendix C's figure is replaced and its panel rows reversed, although Figure 16's caption retains the old top/bottom descriptions. The comprehensive benchmark plots are retained as Figures 17–18.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens empirical scrutiny through alternative projection controls, initialization and centering tests, shifted-optimum experiments and a better-specified GP comparison. These address gaps in v3's evidence for the GI mechanism, while the stated code link improves access information. Gains are tempered by Figure 2(c)'s new ranking/text contradiction and the claim that predictive-mean MSE convergence verifies a stronger mean-and-variance assumption. The net improvement is therefore limited.
